chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fazzal, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked, 'How much is given to the man from the Zakat?' He said:
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'When you give, enrich him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the minimum amount of Zakat to give to ensure the recipient is enriched?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) emphasizes the qualitative impact of Zakat over mere quantitative compliance, advising donors to provide enough to genuinely alleviate poverty. This reflects the Shia scholarly principle that Zakat is a means of social empowerment, ensuring the recipient achieves a degree of self-sufficiency rather than remaining dependent. The directive 'enrich him' underscores the transformative purpose of almsgiving in Islamic economics.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Idreed, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Ahmad Bin Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Fazzal, from Amro Bin Saeed, from Musaddiq Bin Sadaqa, from Ammar Bin Musa, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having been asked, ‘How much can the man give from the Zakāt’. Heasws said:
‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Give him so that he get enriched’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ahmad ibn Idris has narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Ahmad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from ‘Amr ibn Sa‘id from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from ‘Ammar ibn Musa who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was once asked about how much Zakat can be given to one person. He (the Imam) said, that abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘When you pay make him rich.’”
